![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226762/assets/9798487c945153400cf573ab87361d316c21a9040c1e17adf16051843bc9acd3.png)

Find the area of the shaded region that lies between the polar curves $r=\sqrt{3}-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ and $r=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,$ as shown above.
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the values of $\theta $ for which the two curves intersect:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3}-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\sqrt{3} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us two solutions for $\theta \in [-\pi ,\pi ]:$

$$
\theta =-\frac{\pi }{6},\frac{\pi }{6}
$$

To determine which is the inner function and which is the outer, let's draw an arrow from the origin that passes through the shaded region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226762/assets/336b0f0bb8c1d5bba38d2fa5b40a09fb9c76fb4cdd7db21d04ceb14c0816aa52.png)

The arrow

- *enters* the region through the inner function $r=\sqrt{3}-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,$ and

- *leaves* through the outer function $r=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$

To find the area, we use the formula

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}([\text{outer}]^{2}-[\text{inner}]^{2})\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where

$\,$ ${\theta }_{1}=-\frac{\pi }{6},\,$ and $\,{\theta }_{2}=\frac{\pi }{6}.$ 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6}((\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}-(\sqrt{3}-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2})\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta -(3-2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6}(-3+2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[-3\theta {|}_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6}+2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta ){|}_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[-3(\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{\pi }{6})+2\sqrt{3}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{6}))] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[-\pi +2\sqrt{3}(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2})] \\  & =\sqrt{3}-\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
